entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:1
segments:
I am come into my garden; this is the King's answer to the invitation of his bride in the last verse of the preceding chapter, from which it should not have been separated. 
 
  Eat, O friends; the friends of the bridegroom.  See note on

. 
 
Christ is prompt to answer the invitations of his friends, when they are made in sincerity; and his communion with them is "sweeter than honey and the honeycomb."  It is a feast "of fat things, full of marrow of wines on the lees well refined."

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:2
segments:
A new picture begins here.  The bride, for her sinful indolence, is forsaken of her beloved, and seeks him sorrowing. 
 
  I sleep, but my heart waketh; the sleep of God's people is never total, like that of the world.  Though the bride is asleep, yet her heart is awake to hear the call of her beloved. 
 
  Open to me; compare

. 
 
  My head is filled with dew; he pleads what he has undergone for her sake.  The dews of Palestine are very heavy.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:3
segments:
I have put off my coat; the church sunk in carnal ease and security, is reluctant to open to the Saviour. 
 
Spiritual slothfulness has its foundation in the want of fervent love towards Christ, and is therefore exceedingly guilty and offensive in his sight.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:4
segments:
Put in his hand; an earnest token of his desire to enter.  In its spiritual application, it denotes all the ways in which Christ arouses his slumbering people. 
 
Christ is too faithful to leave his church slumbering in sinful inaction.  By mingled judgments and mercies, accompanying his word and Spirit, he will arouse her to a sense of her duty, and bring her to repentance.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:5
segments:
Dropped with myrrh; her penitence is a sweet savor to God. 
 
The fingers of penitent believers drop with sweet-smelling myrrh. Their tears and confessions of sin and works meet for repentance, are most precious in God's sight, and will in due time be rewarded with his returning presence and favor.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:6
segments:
Failed when he spake; spoke a reproving word in withdrawing. 
 
Those who have backslidden from God are often left for a season in darkness, that they thus may feel more deeply the evil of sin, seek Christ more earnestly, and set a higher value upon his love.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:7
segments: When for their sins the Redeemer withdraws his presence from his people, they are helpless, and exposed to injuries and insults from the world that lies in wickedness.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:8
segments: Nothing can compensate the true believer for the loss of Christ's comforting presence, and he will not rest till he has recovered it.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:9
segments: What is thy beloved; this question of the daughters of Zion gives the bride occasion to set forth the excellences of her beloved.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:10
segments:
vv 10.16. 
 
In our Redeemer all excellences meet; he is "the chiefest among ten thousand;" "yea, he is altogether lovely."

entries.title: Song of Solomon 5:12
segments:
By the rivers of waters; which doves love to frequent. 
 
  Washed with milk; this denotes the whiteness of their plumage.  The dove is an emblem of innocence, guilelessness, and purity.
